formula: score = bias + SUM over selected angles of SUM over the five Ptolemaic aspects A of w[angle,A] * cos(angle - A);   p = sigmoid(score)

aspects.why_balanced_matters: SUM_A exp(2iA) = 0 for these five angles, so A'A = (5/2)I and the penalty they induce on each angle's coefficient is exactly (2/5)*lambda*I. Ridge is NOT invariant to the choice of aspect basis -- a set with A'A != cI tilts the fit toward one direction of the sky -- so the balance of these five is the property that makes writing the model in them harmless.
aspects.identity: w[angle,A] = (2/5)*amp*cos(A - ideal_separation), and SUM_A w[angle,A]*cos(theta - A) = amp*cos(theta - ideal_separation). The five weights on an angle are a function of its two free numbers, which is why conjunction and opposition are always exact negatives: cos(theta-180) = -cos(theta).

solver.method: damped Newton on the ridge-penalised logistic objective
solver.note: log-loss plus a positive ridge is strictly convex, so the minimum is unique and does not depend on the starting point; every Newton step is one Cholesky solve and the step is halved until the penalised loss falls.

within_era.note: Inside a single husband-birth decade, couple-weighted: the model reaches 0.5672 where two numbers of age gap reach 0.5662, and handing the age gap to the model moves it to 0.5669. Adding his own and her own natal aspects and the three sum families raised the pooled figure but not this one, which is the honest reading: they bought more calendar, not more astrology.
